fields.title: Identify algorithmic optimization candidates in the Rust implementation

data.text: Reviewing main at 4d7e03ea4d52a806dc5aa126b00af30b9cadb400. Strong candidates: repeated ancestor traversals for readiness, linear dependency-key searches in import planning, rescanning all unresolved imported dependencies on every create, per-event whole-state finalization in bulk close, and repeated reverse-dependency scans for multi-issue details. Release-mode synthetic core probes are in /tmp/beadroll-algorithm-probe.edqzSO. Baseline: 837 of 838 tests passed; listing::tests::in_place_rewrites_reuse_names_but_never_file_identity failed at line 67 and reproduced alone because the equal-length rewrite had identical file timestamps. No product files changed.

Completed performance review of main 4d7e03e. Five candidates, with release-mode medians of 3 synthetic public-core-API runs: (1) import.rs:138-154 scans fresh keys for each dependency, O(N*D), replace with key-to-create-ordinal map; 8k to 16k one-edge records took 515 to 2263 ms. (2) transition.rs:71 calls Tx::state between closes; projection/extend.rs:140 rebuilds every label/child index and :235 sorts all event ids per event; 8k closes took 849 ms individually versus 26 ms in one existing-API batch. (3) replay/apply/create.rs:48 revisits every unresolved edge per create; index by awaited key, preserving retractions; 8k to 16k missing-target creates took 3020 to 12365 ms, versus 10 to 23 ms plain. (4) query.rs:202 repeats ancestor walks and materializes blocker lists for boolean readiness; shared cycle-safe propagation can replace quadratic chain walks; 2k to 4k deep chain took 407 to 1678 ms. (5) view.rs:195 scans all dependency edges per detail; shared reverse index makes multi-show output proportional to matching edges; 4k to 8k sparse issues took 540 to 2328 ms. Full rationale, constraints, runnable harness and CSV are in /tmp/beadroll-algorithm-probe.edqzSO. No Rust code changed; this review does not change accepted full-replay, format or ownership decisions. Baseline failure and isolated reproduction are recorded in the previous comment.

data.reason: Delivered five code-referenced algorithmic optimization candidates on main 4d7e03e, verified scaling with release-mode core probes, and recorded reproducible benchmark artifacts. fields.title: Investigate store cache failures when filesystem timestamps do not change

data.text: Observed during roll-lqjj.15. The pre-change ./check.sh failed listing::tests::in_place_rewrites_reuse_names_but_never_file_identity at crates/beadroll-store/src/listing/tests.rs:67: a same-length in-place rewrite retained identical FileKey fields, including mtime and ctime. The post-change baseline also failed listing::tests::names_are_shared_until_added_removed_or_replaced at line 36: replacing 2.json with 4.json returned the cached 2.json listing. Both failures reproduce together on an untouched git archive of original commit 4d7e03ea4d52a806dc5aa126b00af30b9cadb400. Reproduction: cargo nextest run --manifest-path /tmp/beadroll-import-baseline.a9pVTH/Cargo.toml -p beadroll-store -E "test(/^listing::tests::/)". Log: /tmp/beadroll-import-original-listing-20261013.log. Investigate filesystem timestamp collisions and cache invalidation, rather than merely retrying or weakening these assertions. No store code or tests were changed by the import optimization.

Implementation and documentation are ready in the main working tree, uncommitted. Final workspace baseline: 841 run, 839 passed, 2 failed, 3 skipped; doctests have no cases, 14 infra tests passed. Both failures are store listing/cache tests and reproduce together on an untouched archive of original commit 4d7e03e; tracked separately as roll-lqjj.16. All 137 core tests, formatting, workspace clippy and git diff --check passed. Detailed release results and reproduction commands: /tmp/beadroll-algorithm-probe.edqzSO/IMPORT-RESULTS.txt. Keeping this task open because the repository requires a green baseline and landing on main before closure.

fields.title: Finish only what a batch changed when a projection is extended

fields.notes: Review finding 2: each bulk edit asks for fresh state, and every extend reran replay's whole finishing pass (all labels, the whole parent-child index) and sorted every historical event id again. Measured before the fix: 8,000 closes over 8,000 issues took 16.6 s one event at a time against 0.11 s in one batch; bead close of 2,000 of 4,000 issues took 2.49 s.

data.text: Fixed on branch finish-only-what-a-batch-changed, PR #5. Projection::extend now calls replay::finish_some: it relabels only the issues whose operations change labels, and rebuilds the parent-child index only when an operation changes a dependency edge (relabels/rewires list every Op variant, so the compiler asks an operation added). advance takes new ids into the ascending ids instead of sorting them all again. Measured on 8,000 issues: 8,000 closes one at a time 17.97 s -> 0.048 s, label additions 18.68 s -> 0.050 s; end to end one bead close of 8,000 issues 19.8 s -> 0.7 s. Dependency additions one at a time stay at 5.33 s (the index is still built whole when an edge moves): recorded as a decision in REVIEWING.md section 2, since no command writes many dependency events while reading state between them. New: projection::tests::finished (5 tests, each mutation of the classification caught), cargo xtask timing --extend N, docs/FINDINGS.md Z02. ./check.sh green (857 passed), fmt and clippy clean.

Review of the branch (two independent Claude reviews, then Codex) found four follow-ups, all now fixed and on the branch as commits 1bc41fe and 3bfe10d: V01, finish_some relabelled once per label event instead of once per affected issue, a regression for catch-up batches (8,000 label events on one issue in one batch: 6.32 s -> 0.129 s); V02, the ids were a sorted vector a batch merged into, so a clock rollback or a peer whose clock ran ahead made every write move the whole tail, now a BTreeSet with the same bytes and ENCODING (8,000 closes whose ids sort before every id held: 0.235 s -> 0.048 s, the same as in clock order); V03/V05, the GUARANTEES Known limits entry claimed more than the pass delivers and then omitted creates from the index rebuild; V04, the --extend option had no parse test. Five new tests, two new probe shapes. The review-fix loop reached CONVERGED over 0efc65b..3bfe10d: fmt, clippy and ./check.sh green (862 tests) and two clean terminal reviews with all six acceptance criteria satisfied. Note: the baseline failed once on 'No space left on device' (the machine's ~/.cache/kache was 46G and the disk 100 percent full); it passed on retry after cargo clean. Ledger rows Z02 (corrected) and V01-V05 in docs/FINDINGS.md.

data.reason: A projection now finishes only what a batch changed and holds its event ids in a set, so a command writing one event per issue costs its writes and not the whole state. One bead close naming 8,000 issues of 8,000 went from 19.8 s to 0.7 s; at the projection, 8,000 closes one at a time from 17.97 s to 0.048 s, label additions from 18.68 s to 0.050 s, 8,000 label events on one issue in one batch from 6.32 s to 0.129 s, and closes whose ids sort before every id held from 0.235 s to 0.048 s. Replay, the state every command sees, the projection's bytes, ENCODING and format 1 are unchanged. A batch that creates an issue or writes a dependency still has the whole parent-child index built again, one pass a command, recorded as a decision in docs/REVIEWING.md section 2. Seven new tests, cargo xtask timing --extend N as the probe, ledger rows Z02 and V01-V05. Merged to main as cdf311f (PR #5); CI green on Linux and macOS.

fields.title: Ownership protocol simulation and correctness gaps
fields.description:
Strengthen the evidence that ownership remains correct across competing writers, crashes, lost acknowledgements, stalls, refusals and partitions. The remaining implementation is the simulation and the correctness gaps found by the existing suites.

Simulation, in dependency order:
- roll-k2wy.14.1: introduce the Remote interface together with an in-memory implementation. Link over real git remains the other implementation. Check both against the same fetch/publish sequences, including competing publishers; keep each machine's store files real in a temporary directory.
- roll-k2wy.14.2: run the existing 660 sweep schedules over the simulated remote, model the fault boundaries, and compare each step's outcome and settled state with the real-git sweep. Every injected fault must be shown to have fired.
- roll-k2wy.14.3: explore seeded schedules across machines and actors, with faults repeated and interleaved. Accepted claims must survive failures; stale owners must not invalidate newer ownership or its guarded fields. Reproduce and shrink failures, and report coverage by operation, fault and boundary. Run a small budget in the fast suite and 100,000 to 1,000,000 schedules nightly.

Correctness gaps:
- roll-k2wy.14.6 through .12 and .15: focused ownership and recovery regressions, including local trackers, fence and push failures, offline commands, conflicting attempts, repeated sync-repository damage, update edges and multi-issue close. Reopening through update already has stress coverage under .12.
- roll-k2wy.14.13: lost-claim output is already pinned in both human and JSON snapshots; resolve the remaining decision about the unused EndedClaim rendering helpers.
- roll-k2wy.14.14: choose quarantined duplicate placement canonically when there is no unique own copy, assess projection compatibility, and restore the segment fuzzer's delivery-order comparison for these inputs.

Delivered infrastructure:
- roll-k2wy.14.4 is complete: seeded replay/JSON properties and nightly segment/import fuzzing. The custom JSON parser and its dedicated fuzz target were retired by roll-lqjj.53 when serde_json replaced it; a parser target is no longer a requirement.
- roll-k2wy.14.5 is complete: cargo xtask coverage and nightly coverage artifacts.

The real-git sweep, its variants, stress models, remaining fuzz targets and coverage reports continue to provide evidence alongside the simulation. The correctness-gap tasks can proceed independently of the .1 -> .2 -> .3 simulation chain.
fields.acceptance_criteria:
- The real-git and in-memory remotes run the same protocol functions and pass conformance tests for outcomes, heads and trees, with real-git behavior and established git-count/timing budgets preserved (.1).
- All 660 simulated sweep schedules pass, prove their injected faults fired, and match the real-git sweep's step outcomes and settled states; any intentional difference is explained and recorded (.2).
- Generated schedules are reproducible by seed and failures are shrunk to a minimal reported sequence. A small budget runs in the fast suite; nightly runs at least 100,000 schedules, with a target range up to 1,000,000, and fails for required operation/fault/boundary combinations never exercised (.3).
- Simulation finds no violation: at most one confirmed owner, monotone generations, accepted ownership survives failures, stale owners cannot invalidate newer claims or guarded fields, and views/exports converge after settling.
- The remaining ownership/recovery gaps (.6-.12 and .15) have focused regression evidence; .13's remaining EndedClaim helper decision is implemented and documented. Existing completed coverage is retained.
- Quarantined duplicate placement is independent of journal read order, projection compatibility is addressed, and the segment fuzzer no longer exempts these inputs from its order comparison (.14).
- Completed infrastructure stays operational: nightly segment and importer fuzzing, retained coverage reports, and the real-git sweep/variants and stress models. No custom JSON-parser fuzz target is required (.4 and .5 are already closed).
- The completed changes are on main with the fast baseline green, the stress suite green for protocol changes, and the relevant design, guarantee and changelog documentation updated.

data.text: Scope refreshed at the maintainer request after retiring the custom JSON parser. Renamed the epic to Ownership protocol simulation and correctness gaps; centered the remaining work on .1 -> .2 -> .3, retained the quarantine-ordering fix and ownership/recovery gaps, and recorded .4 fuzzing and .5 coverage as delivered. Removed the obsolete three-target requirement: nightly fuzzing now covers segment and importer. Recorded that .13 already pins human and JSON lost-claim output and that .12 already exercises reopening in the stress suite. Acceptance criteria now cover conformance, differential schedules, reproducibility/shrinking, fault coverage, protocol invariants, remaining regressions and completion on main. The epic remains open for implementation.

fields.title: Resolve unused EndedClaim rendering helpers
fields.description:
The original lost-claim rendering test work is complete on main. PR #33 (roll-lqjj.40, merge f759a0b) added the projection ownership fixtures and the commands::ownership transcript. The transcript's ow-7 scenario pins both human show output ("claim by ... lost to ...") and JSON lost_claims with by, at, held_by and event. The earlier comment saying the human output still needed checking is superseded by this verification.

This chore now covers only the remaining EndedClaim API cleanup in crates/beadroll-core/src/state/claim.rs. EndedClaim::ended and EndedClaim::to_value remain public helpers with no callers in product code outside the helpers themselves. EndedClaim::ending is a separate, used helper.

Check workspace and known downstream callers before changing this public API. Remove the unused rendering helpers if no supported caller or intended API contract requires them; otherwise document the concrete reason to retain them and test the supported behavior. Preserve ownership history and the existing human/JSON output.

The lost-claim fixtures are completed evidence, not new work for this chore.

- Existing ownership-history behavior, human and JSON lost-claim fixtures, and format 1 bytes remain correct.
- Record the decision in docs/REVIEWING.md section 2 and any public API change in CHANGELOG.md; the fast baseline is green and the change is on main.
